From curiosity
to a clear next step.

University of Swat — a focused improvement to programme discovery and admissions preparation.

The student problem

A directory can help students find a course but still leave them unsure what to do next. The goal was to connect discovery with a useful personal plan while clearly separating the concept from official university services.

The design response

Keep Swat's forest green, gold and ivory identity, authentic valley photography and formal typography. Improve the existing journey with small, useful interactions and visible sources.

Discover a programme → Save your choices → Prepare → Official portal

Six practical improvements

  1. A shortlist of up to five programme listings.
  2. A remembered preparation checklist and printable plan.
  3. Source-backed details for six initial programmes.
  4. Removable filters, recovery suggestions and shareable searches.
  5. A direct finder action and tighter mobile spacing.
  6. A concise walkthrough and this presentation sheet.

Trust before decoration

54 undergraduate + 3 postgraduate records preserved. University statistics, the supplied Vice Chancellor message, official portals and image credits remain intact.

No invented deadlines, announcements or eligibility claims. Duration is marked unverified where the reviewed source does not establish it. Saved plans stay in the browser and do not submit an application.

Inspired by academic clarity

Oxford's course discovery, course facts and staged admissions guidance informed the structure. The shortlist and saved checklist are proposals for this project; Oxford's branding and academic content were not copied.

Built for everyday access

Static HTML5, CSS3 and vanilla JavaScript. Complete directory content without JavaScript; keyboard controls, reduced motion and responsive layouts retained.

Verified in Chromium: 42 page/width combinations (360–1440 px), no horizontal overflow; six targeted axe WCAG A/AA runs with no reported violations. Storage failure, reload, multiple tabs, search and print flows tested. Automated checks are not a full accessibility certification.
